rules.title: Ban on rent-setting algorithms
rules.requirement: Jersey City bans rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage for rental housing. The report also describes the ordinance as banning use of certain nonpublic data in revenue-management software.
rules.key_value: Ban on rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage

coverage.other_unresolvable: Coverage depends on use of covered rent-setting or revenue-management software/data; the article does not state precise building or tenancy coverage.
coverage.summary: The ordinance concerns Jersey City rental housing and landlords or multifamily owners using rent-setting algorithm technology, with exact coverage not stated.

rules.exemptions: The article says real estate agents/realtors were excluded from the ordinance; it also notes a requested MLS amendment but does not clearly state that MLS was excluded.
rules.penalty: The article references a $2,000 daily fine.
rules.interaction: The article notes a New Jersey Attorney General rent-fixing lawsuit involving RealPage and major landlords and says the U.S. House was considering banning municipalities from these types of actions.
rules.quoted_span:
The Jersey City Council unanimously approved (9-0) a measure banning rent-setting
   algorithms such as RealPage, as well as increasing benefits for laborers, at last night’s
   meeting.
